case.case_title: Sirimawathie Fernando v. Wickremaratne, Officer in Charge, Police Station, Dehiwela and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 255/98, decided on 7 December 1999

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained lawfully and brought before a judge as required by Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed she was detained unnecessarily and unlawfully for several hours at the police station without legal justification or being brought before a judge.
case_context.respondent_argument: The police denied knowledge of the stay order and justified detention as necessary due to obstruction of official duties.
key_facts: Petitioner was taken to the police station after arrest despite producing a stay order.
Petitioner was kept in custody for several hours without being brought before a judge.
No lawful order authorizing detention was produced by the police.
Petitioner was assaulted and humiliated during detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be brought before a judge and not held without legal order. The Court found that the petitioner was detained without lawful authority and was not brought before a judge promptly, violating this constitutional safeguard.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was detained at the police station for several hours despite the production of a valid stay order and without any legal order authorizing such detention or presentation before a judge.
principles_established: Detention without legal order and without prompt presentation before a judge violates Article 13(2).
Police must respect court orders and ensure detainees' rights are protected.

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner’s fundamental rights under Article 13(2) were violated by the police respondents.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The 1st Respondent was ordered to pay Rs. 30,000 personally as compensation for the violation.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central to the Court’s finding that the petitioner was unlawfully detained without legal order and not brought before a judge, constituting a violation of her fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Despite the production of the stay order, the petitioner was taken to the police station and kept there for several hours without lawful authority or being brought before a judge.
